target_customer: Commercial buyers of AI inference tokens and commercial inference providers in the wholesale capacity market
problem: Inference prices are floating and capacity cannot be reserved or resold at a fixed price, so buyers overpay and providers cannot sell forward.
business_model: Marketplace for forward and reserved inference capacity, buyers pay no fees per company site
product_category: AI compute and inference forward market

founders.name: Ilia Bolgov
education: Maths, Imperial College London (per YC page)

founders.name: Roman Yanushevskyi
education: Math and CS, National University of Singapore (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: IOI gold medalist per YC page.

competitors.name: CME Group with Silicon Data
competitors.what: Cash settled compute futures tied to GPU hour benchmarks
competitors.traction_then: Announced 2026-05, launch pending regulatory approval per sources

competitors.name: ICE with Ornn
competitors.what: Cash settled GPU compute futures on Ornn's compute price index
competitors.traction_then: Announced after CME, no volume found

technical_complexity.rationale: Matching, metering, service level definitions and resale for token delivery are marketplace engineering with some financial infrastructure parts; the team is two people.

defensibility.rationale: Liquidity across buyers and providers could compound, but the product is new and large exchanges target the same instrument.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: CME, ICE and Kalshi each moved into compute forward curves or futures in 2026, though on GPU hours rather than token delivery.

market_need_then: Reported reserved GPU contract prices rose while spot fell (single secondary source), and a 2026-03 arXiv paper proposes token futures, indicating interest in hedging inference cost.

identity.visual_style: Finance infrastructure theme per the site
identity.voice_and_tone: Commodity market framing: 'AI is a commodity.'

branding.community_and_virality: Tech Funding News ran a piece framing it as a futures market for inference around the 2026-08 launch.

brand_strength.rationale: Early press from one trade outlet and a YC launch post. No broader community evidence found.

outcome_analysis: Touchmark is a two person YC Summer 2026 company that launched a forward inference market around 2026-08-14 with Wafer as first provider. It has early institutional backers listed on its site. No failure signals were found. Exchange incumbents entering compute futures and the need for liquidity are the main open risks.
notes: Pre-seed stage and date come from a Nordic9 listing (Inception Fund and a16z scouts, amount N/A); the company site lists backers Inception, Liquid 2, Kima Ventures and Pareto without amounts. A search could not confirm Kima separately. Company site says trades clear 10-60% below retail while YC says 10-30%. The launch date comes from one tracker.
